cards.method: General Bayesian inference via Stan (NUTS-only + convergence gate)
cards.when: an arbitrary generative model in the Stan DSL (custom likelihood/hierarchical/state-space); NUTS + a hard convergence gate
cards.when_not: a regression formula -> #69; a BUGS-style model -> #70; a ready-made model (-> #12/#162); MAP or variational inference (out of scope)

alternatives.criterion: the model can be expressed as a formula (linear/GLM/hierarchical)
BUGS syntax / discrete latent states / custom samplers
a ready-made Bayesian VAR — do not rewrite it in Stan
you want a fast MAP/ADVI instead of a full posterior (out of scope)

output_key_fields: summary: data_frame per parameter (mean/se_mean/sd/quantiles/n_eff/Rhat)
max_rhat in diagnostics: the rank-normalised split-R-hat (the convergence decision)
min_bulk_ess / min_tail_ess in diagnostics: the bulk and tail effective sample sizes
num_divergent in diagnostics: divergent transitions (>0 = a biased posterior)
converged (lgl) + nonconvergence_reasons (chr); object=stanfit (stubbed)
interpretation_traps: the classic Rhat/n_eff columns UNDERSTATE non-convergence — read max_rhat in diagnostics instead
an empty or whitespace-only model_code compiles SILENTLY -> a pre-gate
a missing, NaN or infinite value, or an absent variable, drops the fit into an error mode SILENTLY (hence the universal post-gate)
chains>=1 is not enough: a split-R-hat from a single chain reports converged=True on a bimodal posterior (chains>=2 is mandatory)
the seed is MANDATORY: seeding the process generator does NOT reach Stan's own generator, whose default is random
sources: Vehtari et al 2021 (rank-normalized split-R-hat + Bulk/Tail ESS, Bayesian Analysis 16(2))

cards.when: Bayesian regression as a formula (gaussian/student/bernoulli/poisson/negbinomial/Gamma/lognormal) + informative priors; NUTS + a convergence gate
cards.when_not: a custom generative model -> #68; a BUGS-style or discrete model -> #70; frequentist estimation suffices (-> #46 or plain OLS); multilevel, leave-one-out, splines or GP terms (out of scope)

alternatives.criterion: the model is not a regression (custom likelihood/state-space)
panel regression, frequentist estimation + Hausman
conditional quantiles (growth-at-risk), not a posterior mean

alternatives.alt: a multilevel term (1|g) on this card
alternatives.criterion: hierarchical shrinkage — omitted in v1, re-scope

output_key_fields: summary: posterior_summary data_frame (parameter/Estimate/Est.Error/Q2.5/Q97.5)
fixed: fixef data_frame (population-level coefficients + credible intervals)
diagnostics: max_rhat/min_neff_ratio/n_divergent/n_max_treedepth + echoed family/config
converged (lgl) + nonconvergence_reasons (chr); prior=prior_summary df; object=brmsfit (stubbed)
interpretation_traps: the family given AS A STRING: Gamma resolves to an INVERSE link while the canonical choice here is LOG (a silent change of model)
input that is not a frame is SILENTLY coerced to a matrix; missing values in the model columns are SILENTLY dropped listwise
an entirely undefined R-hat/neff (too few retained draws) comes back as -Inf/+Inf and is caught as HARD non-convergence — otherwise the check would pass vacuously
Est.Error = the posterior SD (NOT a frequentist SE); the uncertainty is the credible interval Q2.5/Q97.5

cards.when: a model in BUGS/JAGS syntax (discrete latent variables/mixtures/custom nodes); injection-safe build + a Gelman R-hat/ESS gate
cards.when_not: a model written directly in Stan -> #68 (NUTS is more efficient); a regression formula -> #69; WAIC, HMC, SMC or custom samplers (out of scope)

alternatives.criterion: continuous parameters, you want efficient NUTS
a regression formula, you do not want BUGS
you ALREADY have draws, only diagnostics are needed

output_key_fields: summary: the pooled summary over all chains (mean/median/sd/credible quantiles)
rhat in convergence: the Gelman PSRF matrix [point estimate / upper bound] + mpsrf + ESS
max_rhat/min_ess/converged in convergence; nonconvergence_reasons, as text
samples: list(chains=matrices, nodes); per_chain_summary; metadata (seed/set_seed/config)
object: compiled model/mcmc/samples (stubbed)
interpretation_traps: INJECTION-SAFE: NEVER model code assembled by string concatenation and then evaluated — a brace-break payload = RCE; parse ONLY
a missing value in the data is SILENTLY treated as a node to be imputed (a hidden parameter); clean the data first
setSeed must be a VECTOR seed+0.(nchains-1); a FRESH compiled pipeline (reusing Cmcmc = non-reproducible)
the initial values must cover ALL top-level stochastic parameters, otherwise a blank start yields NaN samples
the default rhat_threshold=1.1 is looser than the 1.01 used by #68/#69 (a BUGS-era convention)
sources: de Valpine et al. 2017 JCGS 26(2) (programming with models: hierarchical modelling and MCMC)

cards.when: for ANY MCMC draws: rank-normalized split-R-hat + Bulk/Tail ESS + mean/median/sd/mad/quantiles/MCSE per parameter
cards.when_not: you want Geweke/Raftery/Heidelberger/HPD/ACF -> #72; chart data -> #73; the engine already produced the diagnostics

alternatives.criterion: you want Geweke z / Raftery-Lewis / Heidel / HPD / autocorrelation
you want rating tables / chart data for R-hat/neff
the fit object already contains R-hat/ESS

output_key_fields: summary: draws_summary df per variable (mean/median/sd/mad/quantiles/rhat/ess_bulk/ess_tail[/mcse_mean])
nchains/niterations/ndraws/nvariables; variables (chr); probs
degenerate_variables: variables whose R-hat is undefined on finite draws (zero variance)
draws: draws_array
interpretation_traps: the summary measures are passed BY VALUE, never resolved by name: a name lookup can silently bind the wrong function and return nonsense (an R-hat of 999)
a 2D matrix/data_frame input is converted SILENTLY into 1 chain; nchains>=2 is required (a split-R-hat of ~1.0 is silent)
ess_bulk = the reliability of the central estimates; ess_tail = the reliability of the credible-interval edges (a low tail ESS -> bad quantiles)
R-hat>1.01 = non-convergence (Vehtari 2021); the wrapper does NOT gate on a threshold (a valid diagnostic, not an error)
an undefined R-hat is not an error — the parameter is constant (see degenerate_variables)
sources: Vehtari et al 2021 (rank-normalized split-R-hat + Bulk/Tail ESS + MCSE, Bayesian Analysis 16(2))

cards.when: the classical diagnostics set for draws: Gelman-Rubin PSRF/MPSRF, Geweke z, ESS, HPD, Raftery-Lewis, Heidel-Welch, autocorrelation
cards.when_not: you want the rank-normalised R-hat with bulk/tail ESS -> #71; chart data -> #73

alternatives.criterion: the modern rank-normalized R-hat + Bulk/Tail ESS (more reliable)
rating tables / chart data for R-hat/neff
single-chain diagnostics (they do not need >=2 chains)

output_key_fields: gelman_psrf: a matrix [point estimate / upper bound] per parameter; mpsrf (undefined when nvar==1)
geweke_z: a matrix (chain x variable) + a derived p-value, 2*Phi(-|z|)
effective_size: a named vector (POOLED = the sum over chains); hpd_interval: a matrix [lower/upper] on the pooled draws
raftery: the resource matrix (M/N/Nmin/I); heidel: stationarity + halfwidth; autocorr: lags x variables; meta
interpretation_traps: mcmc_effective_size SUMS the per-chain ESS across chains — it is pooled, not per chain (pooled=True)
mcmc_raftery with few draws returns a CHARACTER resmatrix c('Error',Nmin) WITHOUT raising an error -> POST-GATE is_numeric + Nmin
Gelman R-hat>1.1 (strictly 1.01) = non-convergence; Geweke |z|>1.96 = non-stationarity
HPD is computed on the POOLED draws (all chains together), one matrix; prob must be strictly in (0,1) (0/1 -> degenerate/full range)
gelman/bundle require nchain>=2; niter>=10 (the spectral measures are undefined below that); a constant parameter -> singular
sources: Plummer, Best, Cowles & Vines 2006, 6(1):7-11 (convergence diagnosis and output analysis for MCMC)

cards.method: Bayesian visualization DATA extractors (data, not charts)
cards.when: extracting NUMERIC data for diagnostic/PPC charts (intervals/areas/trace/rhat/neff/ppc); the frontend draws them
cards.when_not: raw R-hat/ESS numbers -> #71 posterior; classical diagnostics -> #72 MCMC convergence diagnostics; plot-object-returning functions (excluded); ppc_loo_pit (non-deterministic)

alternatives.criterion: raw R-hat/ESS numbers (not rating tables)
HPD/autocorrelation/Gelman/Geweke diagnostics
it produces the rhat VECTOR that feeds bviz_mcmc_rhat_data

output_key_fields: each extractor returns {data: the frame of plot-ready fields, n: its row count, plus the echoed parameters} -> to_mcp records
mcmc_intervals: parameter/outer_width/inner_width/point_est/ll/l/m/h/hh
mcmc_areas: parameter/interval/interval_width/x/density/scaled_density (default prob_outer=1)
mcmc_rhat/mcmc_neff: diagnostic/parameter/value/rating/description (rating low/ok/high)
ppc_intervals/ribbon: per-obs ll/l/m/h/hh; ppc_stat: per-draw value
interpretation_traps: the B extractors take a precomputed numeric VECTOR (rhat/ess-ratio), NOT a fitted model
pars is always passed as plain text, never as an unevaluated expression
prob>prob_outer -> a SILENT swap; prob=0 is accepted SILENTLY; stat=c('mean','sd') keeps ONLY the first
a missing value in the diagnostic vector SILENTLY drops that parameter (fewer rows); that the replicate matrix has exactly one column per observation is a KEY GATE
the output is long-format data FOR a chart, NOT a convergence diagnosis (that decision belongs to #71/#72)
sources: Gabry, Simpson, Vehtari, Betancourt, Gelman 2019 (Visualization in Bayesian workflow, JRSS-A 182(2))

cards.method: Bayesian Structural Time Series (state specification: local/semilocal trend + seasonal + AR + spike-and-slab regression) with MCMC
cards.when: you want a Bayesian structural decomposition/forecast of a univariate series with explicitly interpretable state components (trend + seasonality + AR) and FULL posterior uncertainty (not a point estimate); or a Bayesian regression on a time series with variable SELECTION through spike-and-slab (expected_model_size) when you have many candidate regressors; you want the posterior mean contribution of each component (nowcasting/decomposition) + predictive quantile bands
cards.when_not: you want a point or frequentist state-space estimate with no MCMC (-> #58/#59, category 10); multivariate or cointegration dynamics (VAR/VECM/Bayesian VAR); a fully custom likelihood or hierarchical model (-> #68/#69/#70); a plain ARIMA or ETS forecast with no component decomposition; a very long series where the MCMC cost is not justified against a fast Kalman filter

alternatives.criterion: you want a Bayesian state-space model with an explicit prior specification / custom observation models (SV/non-Gaussian) rather than the flag-driven structural builder
you want a point/frequentist MLE state-space model (a fast Kalman filter, no MCMC) — the same structural decomposition without posterior draws
you need a fully custom hierarchical/state model that cannot be expressed with the BSTS state components
outliers / heavy tails in the observation — a robust observation model instead of gaussian
long forecast horizons — a mean-reverting slope avoids the explosive trend of the local linear model

output_key_fields: bsts_fit: state_components (the component names — trend, seasonal, AR, regression); residual_sd (the posterior mean observation sigma); sigma_obs_quantiles; coefficients {variable, inclusion_prob, posterior_mean, posterior_mean_incl} for the regression only; burn; fitted_series with its time index; plus the handle
bsts_predict: mean/median (chart-data); lower/upper predictive bands at the quantiles; step; has_regression
bsts_components: contributions (time x component posterior mean; a stacked decomposition); contributions_lower/upper bands; components; time; burn
interpretation_traps: DETERMINISM: this is MCMC with its own compiled generator — reproducibility requires seeding BOTH the process generator and the sampler itself; the wrapper does both, in the fit AND in the prediction, and the seed is MANDATORY

local_linear_trend vs semilocal: the local linear trend has a random-walk slope that can 'explode' at long horizons; the semilocal one (an AR(1) mean-reverting slope) is safer for forecasting — the two are mutually exclusive (gate)

inclusion_prob (spike-and-slab): the posterior probability that the regressor is in the model; posterior_mean is the MEAN OVER ALL draws (it includes the zeros -> shrunk), posterior_mean_incl is conditional on inclusion — do NOT confuse them
expected_model_size applies ONLY in regression mode; it sets the prior number of non-zero coefficients (smaller => a stronger sparsity prior); in a pure structural model it is an error (gate)
regression forecast: newdata (the future regressors) is MANDATORY and must have nrow==horizon with the same predictor columns — otherwise a gate stop (the forecast needs future values of X)
burn-in: the default SuggestBurn(0.1) discards 10% as warm-up; too few niter => unstable posterior means; keep niter large enough (>=500 in production; 100-250 only for smoke tests)
seasonal.N.k naming: AddSeasonal with nseasons=12 gives the component 'seasonal.12.1'; season_duration>1 groups steps into a season (e.g. weekly seasonality in daily data)
sources: Scott & Varian (2014) Predicting the present with Bayesian structural time series, Int. J. Mathematical Modelling and Numerical Optimisation 5:4-23
Scott & Varian (2015) Bayesian Variable Selection for Nowcasting Economic Time Series, in Economic Analysis of the Digital Economy (NBER/Univ. Chicago Press)
Brodersen, Gallusser, Koehler, Remy & Scott (2015) Inferring causal impact using Bayesian structural time-series models, Annals of Applied Statistics 9:247-274
Durbin & Koopman (2012) Time Series Analysis by State Space Methods, 2nd ed., Oxford University Press (structural components + the Kalman filter foundation)
George & McCulloch (1997) Approaches for Bayesian variable selection, Statistica Sinica 7:339 (the spike-and-slab prior)
precondition_tools: bsts_fit (the PRODUCER: it builds the state specification from the flags, runs the MCMC fit, and returns the object handle that predict and components consume — the seed is MANDATORY)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the data_frame for regression mode: response + regressors)
c10_trend_cycle_statespace/kalman_filter_smoother.kf_local_linear_trend (a frequentist state-space baseline; compare before investing in MCMC)

cards.method: Sequential Monte Carlo / particle filters for non-linear/non-Gaussian state-space models (bootstrap / auxiliary / Liu-West / ensemble Kalman)
cards.when: you have a BUGS-style state-space (hidden Markov) model with latent states x[t] and observations y[t]; you want (a) an estimate of the marginal log-likelihood (for model comparison / particle MCMC / likelihood-based inference) and/or (b) the filtered distribution of the latent states f(x[t]|y[1:t]) per time point (mean/quantiles = chart-data). It handles NON-linear/NON-Gaussian transition & observation equations where the Kalman filter does not apply
cards.when_not: a linear-Gaussian state-space model (use the exact Kalman filter of #58/#59/#61 — analytic, with no Monte Carlo noise); you want a FULL Bayesian posterior over the parameters with MCMC diagnostics (-> #70, which gates on Rhat and ESS); structural-break or latent-regime work (category 06); simple smoothing with no latent-state model (-> #56)

alternatives.criterion: a linear-Gaussian SSM -> an exact Kalman filter/smoother (no Monte Carlo variance), a closed-form likelihood
you want a full Bayesian posterior over the parameters + convergence diagnostics (Rhat/ESS), not only latent-state filtering / a log_lik
a peaked/informative observation likelihood -> lookahead resampling reduces particle degeneracy relative to bootstrap
you want joint state+parameter online estimation in ONE pass (caution: didactic, often poor; no log_lik)
a high-dimensional latent state with additive normal observation error -> an EnKF Monte Carlo Kalman approximation (no log_lik)

output_key_fields: method: the selected filter; latent_vars: the names of the latent variable(s)

log_likelihood + log_likelihood_available: the estimated marginal log-likelihood (numeric for the bootstrap and auxiliary filters; blank with the flag False for the Liu-West and ensemble-Kalman filters — STRUCTURALLY so, never a fabricated value)
state_summary: a data_frame {node, mean, sd, q..} PER latent node/time — the per-time filtered summaries (chart-data); state_mean: the per-time posterior mean
filtered_samples: a named list of equally weighted samples (particles × latent nodes) per latent variable — for downstream reweighting/plots
ess + ess_available: the per-time effective sample size (numeric for the bootstrap and auxiliary filters; absent, with the flag False, otherwise)
param_summary + param_vars: for the Liu-West filter ONLY, the posterior summary of the top-level parameters; absent for the rest
n_particles / n_time / metadata (method/thresh/lookahead/d/seed/saveAll)
interpretation_traps: METHOD HETEROGENEITY (live-verified): ONLY the bootstrap and auxiliary filters return a log-likelihood estimate and a per-time ESS; the Liu-West and ensemble-Kalman filters return neither. The node declares this explicitly through log_likelihood_available and ess_available — do not read a blank log-likelihood as 'a bad model'; it is a structural limit of the method

particle depletion: too few particles, or a model-data mismatch, gives a log-likelihood of minus infinity or NaN samples; the node blocks it with a hard gate. Raise nParticles (default 1000); the log-likelihood estimate carries Monte Carlo variance, so model comparison must use the SAME seed and particle count

the Liu-West filter: its own documentation warns that it 'often performs poorly, provided primarily for didactic purposes'; the parameter posteriors can be over-concentrated (particle impoverishment). Prefer particle MCMC (outside the surface), or #70, for reliable parameter inference
filtered, NOT smoothed: what comes back is f(x[t]|y[1:t]) (saveAll=True, smoothing=False); it is not the full smoothing distribution f(x[t]|y[1:T])

thresh MUST ==1 (gate): resampling at every step => mvEWSamples is equally weighted everywhere => correct per-time summaries; thresh<1 is blocked (silently wrong otherwise); this applies ONLY to bootstrap (auxiliary ignores thresh)

latentNodes in TIME order: they must be stochastic nodes (for instance 'x' or 'x[1:10]'); the data must contain NO gaps, since a gap is treated as a node to be imputed — a hidden parameter, hence the gate
sources: Michaud, de Valpine, Turek, Paciorek & Nguyen 2021 JSS 100(3) (sequential Monte Carlo methods)
Gordon, Salmond & Smith (1993) 'Novel approach to nonlinear/non-Gaussian Bayesian state estimation', IEE Proc. F 140(2):107 (the bootstrap filter)
Pitt & Shephard (1999) 'Filtering via simulation: Auxiliary particle filters', JASA 94(446):590 (the auxiliary filter)
Liu & West (2001) 'Combined parameter and state estimation in simulation-based filtering', in Sequential Monte Carlo Methods in Practice, Springer, pp.197-223
Houtekamer & Mitchell (1998) 'Data assimilation using an ensemble Kalman filter technique', Monthly Weather Review 126(3):796
Doucet, de Freitas & Gordon (2001) Sequential Monte Carlo Methods in Practice, Springer
precondition_tools: smc_filter (the default method=bootstrap; only bootstrap/auxiliary return log_lik+ESS)
c14_bayesian_toolkit/general_bugs_style.bugs_style_mcmc (the same BUGS DSL; for a full parameter posterior rather than filtering)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the observations y as a series)

cards.method: LOO-CV, WAIC, model comparison and stacking weights
cards.when: comparing Bayesian models by their predictive performance rather than by in-sample fit, and combining them when none dominates
cards.when_not: the models have different likelihoods or different data, where the criteria are not comparable

alternatives.criterion: the default, with a built-in reliability diagnostic
cheaper but less reliable
you want a combination rather than a selection

output_key_fields: elpd_loo, elpd_waic: expected log predictive density with standard errors
pareto_k: the reliability diagnostic -- values above 0.7 mean the estimate is untrustworthy
weights: stacking or pseudo-BMA weights
comparison: models ranked with differences and their standard errors
interpretation_traps: PARETO K ABOVE 0.7 MEANS THE LOO ESTIMATE IS UNRELIABLE for that observation, and reporting elpd without checking k is the standard misuse of this diagnostic
the standard error of a difference in elpd is what decides whether models are distinguishable; a ranking without it is not evidence
LOO assumes observations are exchangeable, which time series and hierarchical structures violate -- leave-future-out is the analogue there

cards.method: Bayes factors, Savage-Dickey ratios and ROPE decisions
cards.when: quantifying evidence for a point null, or deciding whether an effect is practically equivalent to zero
cards.when_not: the priors are vague, where Bayes factors are dominated by the prior width and are not interpretable

alternatives.criterion: evidence for a point null against an alternative
nested models, cheap to compute from the posterior
you want a practical-equivalence decision rather than evidence

output_key_fields: bayes_factor: evidence ratio, with the prior it depends on stated
savage_dickey: the prior-to-posterior density ratio at the null
rope_probability: posterior mass inside the region of practical equivalence
decision: accept, reject or undecided
interpretation_traps: BAYES FACTORS ARE ACUTELY SENSITIVE TO THE PRIOR WIDTH on the tested parameter -- widening a vague prior can move the factor by orders of magnitude with no change in the data
the ROPE must be set from substantive knowledge before seeing the posterior; choosing it afterwards makes the decision circular
the Savage-Dickey ratio needs the prior density at the null to be well estimated, which fails for improper priors
sources: Kruschke 2018 (Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science 1:270)

cards.method: Variational inference, Pathfinder and Laplace approximation
cards.when: the posterior is needed faster than sampling allows, or the model is too large for a Markov chain to mix
cards.when_not: you need accurate tail or correlation estimates, which every approximation here understates

alternatives.criterion: accuracy matters more than speed
a fast approximate posterior
the posterior is near-Gaussian around the mode

output_key_fields: approximation: the fitted approximate posterior
elbo: the evidence lower bound path, whose convergence must be checked
psis_k: diagnostic for how good the approximation is
comparison: against a short MCMC run where available
interpretation_traps: MEAN-FIELD VARIATIONAL INFERENCE SYSTEMATICALLY UNDERSTATES POSTERIOR VARIANCE and destroys correlations between parameters -- credible intervals from it are too narrow, often severely
a converged ELBO does not mean a good approximation; it means the optimiser stopped, and the PSIS diagnostic is what actually assesses quality
Laplace approximation is only defensible when the posterior really is near-Gaussian, which multimodality and boundaries break
sources: Zhang, Carpenter, Gelman & Vehtari 2022 (Journal of Machine Learning Research 23:1)

cards.when: choosing priors deliberately and checking what they imply about the data before any data is seen
cards.when_not: the priors are fixed by convention or a referee; the model is too complex to simulate from the prior

alternatives.criterion: check what the prior implies for observables
you know plausible ranges, not distributions
you want minimal influence

output_key_fields: prior_predictive: simulated observables under the prior
elicited: the distribution matching stated quantiles
implied_range: what the prior implies for the data scale
warnings: priors implying impossible or absurd observables
interpretation_traps: A 'VAGUE' PRIOR ON A COEFFICIENT CAN BE WILDLY INFORMATIVE ON THE OUTCOME SCALE, especially with a nonlinear link -- the prior predictive check is how that is caught
priors that put mass on impossible observables (negative prices, probabilities above one) are common and are not harmless
eliciting from quantiles requires the elicited quantiles to be internally consistent, which they frequently are not

cards.when: you want flexible nonparametric regression with honest uncertainty, without choosing a functional form or tuning a penalty
cards.when_not: the relationship is known to be linear; interpretability of individual terms is required

alternatives.criterion: the form is known
flexible, with posterior uncertainty
prediction only, no uncertainty needed

output_key_fields: posterior_predictive: draws of the fitted surface
variable_inclusion: how often each covariate is split on
partial_dependence: marginal effect curves with credible bands
convergence: chain diagnostics on the tree ensemble
interpretation_traps: VARIABLE INCLUSION FREQUENCIES ARE NOT VARIABLE IMPORTANCE and are biased toward covariates with many possible split points
BART's default priors are calibrated for standardised outcomes; on an unstandardised scale they can be strongly informative
convergence diagnostics for tree ensembles are weaker than for parametric models -- the usual R-hat on individual trees is meaningless
sources: Chipman, George & McCulloch 2010 (Annals of Applied Statistics 4:266-298)
Hill, Linero & Murray 2020 (Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application 7:251)

cards.method: Gaussian-process regression and Bayesian nonparametric trends
cards.when: a smooth latent function with calibrated uncertainty, where the uncertainty must widen honestly away from the data
cards.when_not: the sample is large enough that the cubic cost is prohibitive without approximation; the function is not smooth

alternatives.criterion: cheaper, similar smoothness
you want a full posterior over functions
the sample is large

output_key_fields: posterior_mean, posterior_band: the latent function and its uncertainty
hyperparameters: length scale, amplitude and noise
log_marginal_likelihood: for kernel comparison
extrapolation_warning: where the posterior reverts to the prior
interpretation_traps: A GAUSSIAN PROCESS REVERTS TO ITS PRIOR MEAN AWAY FROM THE DATA, so extrapolated forecasts drift to the mean with wide bands -- that is correct behaviour and is frequently mistaken for a bug
the kernel is the model; a squared-exponential kernel assumes infinite differentiability, which is wrong for most economic series -- Matern is usually the better default
hyperparameters estimated by marginal likelihood can land in a local optimum that oversmooths dramatically
sources: Rasmussen & Williams 2006, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning
Roberts et al. 2013 (Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A 371:20110550)
